info.title: Adamant HTTP surface
info.summary: Every route handler under src/app/api, as a contract a change can be compared against.
info.description:
HALF OF THIS DOCUMENT IS DERIVED AND HALF IS WRITTEN, AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT.

Derived and pinned by `npm run api:surface:check` (blocking, through test-unit/api-surface.test.mjs inside `npm run test:unit`): the path template, the exported verbs, the path parameters, `x-adamant.source`, `x-adamant.auth` and `x-adamant.maxDuration`. Those six facts are read out of the tree by scripts/lib/api-surface-core.mjs on every build, and a disagreement between them and this file fails the build. Editing this half by hand to make a red check green is the one thing never to do here — the disagreement IS the change being caught. Regenerate with `npm run api:surface:write`, which keeps every written sentence, and read the diff.

Written and required: the one-sentence `summary` on every operation. Not generated, because a generated sentence about a route reads as informative and says nothing; not optional either, because the check refuses a `TODO` summary, which is what a route arriving for the first time is given.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED YET. Request and response BODIES. Every operation below states its posture's response codes, and those are indicative rather than derived — the check does not compare them against the handler. Pinning bodies means either a schema per route hand-written from 88 modules (documentation that goes stale the first week) or a type extractor (a real project, and a bigger one than the gap this closes). The honest position is that the SHAPE of the surface — what exists, what verbs it answers, and who it lets in — is pinned today, and the bodies are not. If a body contract starts mattering to a consumer, the seam to extend is `compareSurface()` in scripts/lib/api-surface-core.mjs, not this file.

AUTH IS THE FACT WORTH HAVING HERE. `x-adamant.auth` is classified by the SAME regex `scripts/sast.mjs` uses for its `route-auth` rule, deliberately copied rather than re-invented, so the document and the security gate cannot hold two opinions about whether a handler establishes caller identity. A route that quietly stops requiring a session changes one word in this file and fails the build.

sessionCookie.name: authjs.session-token
sessionCookie.description: An Auth.js v5 session established by Google OAuth. The tenant key is derived from the session (`u_{userId}_proj_{projectId}`) and never taken from the wire — an unverified projectId does not mint a tenant.

cronBearer.description: The CRON_SECRET bearer token, compared in constant time by src/lib/cron-auth.ts. Vercel's scheduler holds it; so does whatever uptime monitor polls /api/health.

pathToken.name: token
pathToken.description: A 128-bit random token carried as a PATH segment, not a query parameter — OpenAPI has no place to say that, so this scheme is documentation. The token is the credential: unguessable, per-resource, revocable by re-minting, and the (userId, projectId) pairing is read from the stored row rather than supplied by the caller.

Ok.description: The resource, in the route's own envelope (`{ ok: true, … }` for most of the app surface).

Created.description: Created — the new resource is in the body.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be read: a malformed body, a missing or unparseable parameter.

Unauthorized.description: No caller identity: no session, or a CRON_SECRET bearer token that did not match.

Forbidden.description: Identified, but not entitled to this resource.

NotFound.description: No such resource for this caller. Ownership failures answer here rather than leaking existence.

Conflict.description: The resource is already in the state the request would create, or a concurrent write won.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body exceeded this route's byte cap.

Unprocessable.description: Read, but refused: a field is missing, out of range, or names something the route will not act on.

TooManyRequests.description: A durable per-IP limit or the global daily spend ceiling refused the call (src/lib/ai/durable-limit.ts).

ServerError.description: An unhandled failure on this side.

BadGateway.description: An upstream — a provider, an ad platform, an image service — failed or timed out.

Text.description: A plain-text body. The caller is a robot, not a browser, so there is no JSON envelope.

An empty catalog answers with a VALID EMPTY feed rather than a 404, because every one of these channels de-lists a shop whose feed errors; only an unknown or revoked token is a 404.

get.summary: The operator readiness probe: which credentials are configured, whether Firestore answers a one-document read, and which crons have gone stale.
get.description: Behind the same CRON_SECRET bearer guard as the crons, so it is safe to wire to an uptime monitor. It reports WHICH credentials are present as booleans and never a value. `firestoreReachable` is reality rather than configuration — a present-but-misconfigured credential passes the boolean and fails here — and `cronsStale` names the schedules whose last run is older than vercel.json allows.

parameters.description: The 128-bit per-(project, channel) intake token. Half of the credential; the other half is an HMAC over the raw body.

get.summary: Answer a channel's subscription verification handshake (Meta's hub.challenge).

post.summary: Accept an inbound message from a channel webhook and append it to the project's twin inbox as a pending draft.
post.description: Deliberately anonymous — the callers are machines — with the reasoning in .github/security/sast-allowlist.json § route-auth. The order of operations IS the security property: read the RAW body, cap it at 64 KB, verify the HMAC over those exact bytes, and only THEN parse. It cannot send, approve, mint sentAt, or read anything back; the worst a stolen token buys is unread messages in one project's inbox, bounded at INBOUND_PENDING_CAP with operator-written drafts never evicted.
